title: Hardening hosted GPU capacity: queued-request fanout, admission control, and backpressure hardening
creator: Aisha Chen
description: Follow-up ticket from the hosted API GPU capacity exhaustion event on 2026-03-03. Customers saw long tail latency and 429 throttles as request queues accumulated on a small subset of GPU hosts. This ticket coordinates engineering work to add a lightweight admission controller, improve request fanout and dequeue behavior, and extend autoscaler signals to include enqueue depth so scaling reacts earlier. Goals: reduce tail latency under bursty loads, prevent queue amplification after partial failures, and ensure predictable degradation (graceful shedding + fallback).
postmortem_summary: On 2026-03-03 a model rollout produced an unexpected high-average-token workload that persisted for ~45 minutes. Autoscaler relied on GPU utilization only and did not scale fast enough; queue depth on several hosts exceeded limits causing per-host dequeue stalls and request retries. Some requests were reissued by upstream LB which amplified load on the remaining healthy hosts. Contributing factors: (1) lack of enqueue-depth signal in scaling, (2) no global admission/fairness layer leading to head-of-line blocking for small requests, (3) retry amplification from the API gateway. We restored capacity via emergency scale-up and targeted evictions, and implemented temporary rate limits; this ticket implements durable fixes.
actions: Implement lightweight admission controller (token-bucket per-customer + global max-inflight) in front of GPU queues. Owner: Marcus. Due: 2026-03-18. Deliverable: config flag to enable per-customer buckets and emergency 'circuit' for overload.

Add enqueue-depth telemetry and expose new metric 'gpu.queue_depth_90p' to autoscaler input. Owner: SRE team (Elena Ruiz). Due: 2026-03-14. Deliverable: Grafana panel + alert on sustained queue_depth > 100 for 2 minutes.

Extend autoscaler policy to consider combined signal: moving-average(utilization, 30s) + short-window(queue depth). Change: reduce scale-up cooldown to 30s when queue depth spike detected. Owner: Autoscale squad (Kenji Ito). Due: 2026-03-20.
Implement bounded fanout when dequeueing from overloaded GPUs: prefer local dequeue and avoid synchronous retries across all replicas. Owner: Runtime team (Priya Nair). Due: 2026-03-16.

Add early-shed policy for requests exceeding 95th percentile waiting time with structured fallback (try smaller model variant or return structured rate-limit response with Retry-After). Owner: API team (Rafael Gomez). Due: 2026-03-15.

Create synthetic chaos test (burst + partial host failure) in our staging scale test harness to validate backpressure behavior and autoscaler response. Owner: Test-infra (Maya Singh). Due: 2026-03-22.
Update incident runbook with explicit checklist for GPU queue saturation: detection, emergency scale, selective eviction, and stakeholder comms. Owner: Incident Ops (Tom Baker). Due: 2026-03-12.
Postmortem and customer-facing incident note drafted and reviewed; schedule CS/AE sync to discuss credits and follow-up. Owner: Aisha Chen. Due: 2026-03-13.
Open follow-on design doc for long-term fairness routing (per-customer weighted scheduling across GPU pools). Owner: Platform Architect (Dr. Nina Park). Due: 2026-04-02.
progress_updates: 2026-03-05: Ticket created after incident postmortem call. Immediate mitigations (temporary per-API rate limits) already applied by SRE.

2026-03-06: Telemetry spike confirmed; dash: https://grafana.redwood.company/d/queues/hosted-gpu-queues incident-2026-03-03. Linked PR for temporary rate-limit: https://github.com/redwood-inference/proxy/pull/4127.

2026-03-08: Design review for admission controller held with runtime, autoscale, and API teams; decision to keep controller state minimal (token buckets + global max-inflight) to avoid central coordination.

2026-03-10: Prototype admission gate merged behind feature flag: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1983. Initial smoke tests in staging show 30% reduction in tail p99 latency for microbursts.
2026-03-11: Autoscaler metrics change under review: PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/autoscale/pull/287. Waiting on SRE sign-off for new alert thresholds.
2026-03-11: Runbook draft uploaded: https://confluence.redwood.company/display/OPS/GPU+Queue+Saturation+Runbook. Assigned owner for runbook maintenance.
acceptance_criteria: Admission controller rolled out behind feature flag and validated against staging chaos test (no >2x retry amplification observed).
Autoscaler reacts to queue-depth spikes within 60s in staging; production rollout reduces tail latency p99 by >=20% during simulated burst without increasing cost >5%.
Runbook updated and on-call trained (one pager + playbook).
Synthetic chaos test added to CI with nightly runs and a dashboard for historical regressions.
notes: Keep feature-flagged rollout for first two weeks with tight telemetry. Coordinate with CS on customer remediation. Consider temporary migration to dedicated pools for high-SLA customers if recurrence risk remains.
